The primary buggy method is `org.jfree.data.DefaultKeyedValues.removeValue(int)`.

Diagnosis:
- It removes entries from `keys` and `values`, but only rebuilds `indexMap` when `index < this.keys.size()`.
- After removing the last remaining item, `this.keys.size()` becomes `0`, so `rebuildIndex()` is skipped.
- That leaves a stale mapping in `indexMap`, so `getIndex("K1")` returns `0` even after `"K1"` was removed.
- Later, `setValue()` trusts that stale index and executes `this.keys.set(0, key)` / `this.values.set(0, value)` on empty lists, causing the observed `IndexOutOfBoundsException`.

This explains:
- `testGetIndex2()`: removed key still resolves to index `0` instead of `-1`.
- `testRemoveColumnByKey()` and `testBug1835955()`: removing column `"C2"` clears row data but leaves stale row key indexes; adding `"C2"` again hits `DefaultKeyedValues.setValue()` with invalid index `0`.

There is also a separate contract bug in `org.jfree.data.DefaultKeyedValues.removeValue(java.lang.Comparable)`:
- Its Javadoc says it should throw `UnknownKeyException` for an unrecognised key.
- The implementation silently returns when `getIndex(key) < 0`.
- That is why `testRemoveValue()` fails.

- After removing the last remaining item, `this.keys.size()` becomes `0`, so `rebuildIndex()` is skipped.
- That leaves a stale mapping in `indexMap`, so `getIndex("K1")` returns `0` even after `"K1"` was removed.
- Later, `setValue()` trusts that stale index and executes `this.keys.set(0, key)` / `this.values.set(0, value)` on empty lists, causing the observed `IndexOutOfBoundsException`.

This explains:
- `testGetIndex2()`: removed key still resolves to index `0` instead of `-1`.
- `testRemoveColumnByKey()` and `testBug1835955()`: removing column `"C2"` clears row data but leaves stale row key indexes; adding `"C2"` again hits `DefaultKeyedValues.setValue()` with invalid index `0`.

There is also a separate contract bug in `org.jfree.data.DefaultKeyedValues.removeValue(java.lang.Comparable)`:
- Its Javadoc says it should throw `UnknownKeyException` for an unrecognised key.
- The implementation silently returns when `getIndex(key) < 0`.
- That is why `testRemoveValue()` fails.
